summaryTab.matchCommentary:
The Test match at Kensington Oval commenced with high tactical intensity as West Indies posted 204/10 (69.3 ov) in their opening innings. In response, Sri Lanka countered with 154/10 (58.6 ov), setting the stage for a compelling contest of tactical endurance. Early sessions tested batting resolve against disciplined seam movement, with both attacks striving to gain the upper hand on a developing surface.

The defining turning point arrived during Collapse: Lost 10 Wickets for 92 Runs, which irrevocably altered the trajectory of the match. As the match progressed through its pivotal middle stages, JO Holder delivered a masterclass for West Indies (89 Runs & 9 Wkts), absorbing intense pressure and tilting the momentum decisively. Crucial partnership stands and incisive bowling spells broke the opposition's resistance, shifting the control share (Sri Lanka 45%) and allowing Sri Lanka to dictate terms heading into the decisive sessions.

Entering the final innings, West Indies faced an uphill battle under unrelenting scoreboard pressure. Sri Lanka's bowling unit, bolstered by CBRLS Kumara (7 Wickets), maintained relentless discipline and attacked the stumps relentlessly. Wicket clusters in the closing sessions dismantled any remaining resistance, sealing Sri Lanka won by 4 wickets in comprehensive fashion.

Verdict: Sri Lanka's triumph was built on superior pressure absorption, clinical execution during critical moments, and the ability to dominate key sessions. While West Indies produced fighting phases, Sri Lanka won the pivotal turning points and sustained higher tactical control across all five days to emerge as deserved victors.
